title: Tesla renames 'Full Self-Driving' to 'Tesla Assisted Driving' in Europe
key_facts: Tesla has renamed its driver-assistance system in Europe from 'Full Self-Driving (Supervised)' to 'Tesla Assisted Driving' after pushback from Germany's transportation ministry.
Germany's transport minister Steffen Bilger said earlier this month that the name 'Full Self-Driving' was somewhat misleading because the software does not perform the entire task of driving.
Bilger spoke with Tesla last month and the company suggested the name change, according to an official ministry release.
Bilger will now advocate for approval of Tesla Assisted Driving across Europe ahead of an EU-wide vote that could happen later this year.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk thanked Bilger on X this week.
The system still requires humans to pay attention to the road and take over when necessary.
The Netherlands was the first European country to approve FSD (Supervised), a few weeks after March 2026.

On Wednesday (7 Oct 2026) Reuters reported that Tesla's campaign for European approval was built on faulty company safety research and flawed studies, and that Dutch regulator RDW faced fierce pressure from Tesla and its online supporters.
quote_evidence: Tesla has changed the name of its advanced driver assistance system in Europe after pushback from Germany's transportation ministry.
Germany's transport minister, Steffen Bilger, said earlier this month that calling the software "Full Self-Driving" was somewhat misleading because it doesn't perform the entire task of driving.
Bilger said he will now advocate for approval of Tesla Assisted Driving across Europe ahead of an EU-wide vote that could happen later this year.
why_it_matters_hint: A regulator pressed a rename that stresses drivers must stay in charge, and the minister now backs EU-wide approval, which Tesla wants for wider sales of the feature in Europe.
